source_contract_findings.row_semantics: one row per offense charge within a crime incident; multiple charges can share an incident number
notes: Detroit's public crime-viewer page resolves to a city-operated ArcGIS incident service rather than only a narrative dashboard.
The exact public 2024 bulk service is now pinned at the RMS Crime Incidents 2024 FeatureServer.
The exact public machine contract is the FeatureServer query endpoint rather than an inferred static CSV URL.
The service exposes point geometry, latitude/longitude, nearest intersection, police precinct, neighborhood, and a 2020 census block GEOID.
The service description states that incident locations are generalized to the nearest intersection for privacy and that each row represents one offense charge tied to a crime incident.

The packet is no longer blocked on source discovery; it is now a doctrine decision about whether the row-per-charge public feed can be defended against the official victim-based and vehicle-based year-end anchors.

Extract-backed code-plus-description review materially tightened several Detroit families: rape lands at 614 unique reports versus the official 616, motor-vehicle theft at 8,308 versus 8,408, and burglary at 4,642 versus 4,766, while aggravated assault and larceny remain materially off.

The current clean judgment is negative for city-share promotion: only burglary and secondarily robbery are semantically plausible incident-style report-dedupe comparators, and neither clears the repo promotion bar.

why_not: The packet offense crosswalk is now sharp enough for review, but the public feed is still row-per-charge while the official anchors are partly victim-based or vehicle-based.

Rape and motor-vehicle theft are near exact numerically under description-filtered report-deduped candidates, but they are not semantically exact-comparable because the official anchors are victim-based or vehicle-based.
Burglary and robbery are the only incident-style report-dedupe comparators that are semantically plausible, and they still land at 4,642 vs 4,766 and 1,269 vs 1,210 respectively.
No offense currently has an exact-comparable packet line that satisfies the repo's offense-selective promotion bar.

notes: The official 2024 Detroit year-end table exposes all seven repo offense families.
The service-level offense ontology is rich enough to support a seven-offense crosswalk, but it is not a clean one-column mapping.

Observed category mismatches are now concrete rather than speculative: homicide rows include negligent homicide variants; robbery includes carjacking; burglary includes entry-without-permission rows; sexual-assault-related rows are split across SEXUAL ASSAULT and SEX OFFENSES; and the official year-end table treats homicide, sex assault, and aggravated assault as victim-based and motor-vehicle theft as vehicle-based.

Extract-backed code-plus-description review now makes the outlook more specific: rape and motor_vehicle_theft are near exact numerically under description-filtered report-deduped candidates, but they stay semantically blocked because the official anchors are victim-based or vehicle-based.
Burglary is the cleanest incident-style report-deduped candidate and robbery is a secondary incident-style candidate, but both still miss the repo promotion bar numerically.

sources: Detroit Police Department 2024 Year End Stats
notes: The official year-end PDF includes a page-4 Part 1 offense table with 2023 and 2024 counts for homicide, sex assault, aggravated assault, robbery, burglary, larceny, and motor vehicle theft.
The packet now carries those extracted rows in published_reference_extract.csv and reconciliation_summary.csv.
The counts are labeled preliminary, with homicide, sex assault, and aggravated assault footnoted as victim-based and motor vehicle theft footnoted as vehicle-based.
Even if the within-city share lane stalls, the same official table is a plausible local_publication annual control candidate.

why_not_ready: Victim-based and vehicle-based official counting semantics are not defendably matched against the row-based or report-deduped incident-charge export.
The only incident-style report-dedupe comparators that are semantically plausible, burglary and robbery, still do not clear the repo promotion bar numerically.
No offense currently has an extract-backed exact-comparable packet line that clears the repo's offense-selective promotion bar.
minimum_change_to_unblock: Only reopen Detroit as a live city-share candidate if a future packet review yields an incident-style offense that is both semantically defendable and numerically within the repo bar.
Do not add a generic report-number-dedupe loader path unless that future packet outcome actually requires live code support.
Until then, treat the official Detroit year-end table as the packet's usable bounded annual anchor rather than a city-share promotion lane.
